jess (Docs): Heads-up — I'm opening a short thread to align language for the audit export / retention section in the security docs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4567. Need signoff on phrasing around export retention windows and an edge-case for rotated KMS keys.

omar (Security): Thanks Jess. Quick note: we should avoid the term 'permanent export' — suggest 'export retained until X or customer-requested deletion'. Also: call out the behavior when KMS rotates (decryption still possible for existing exports if key versions are preserved).

maria (Legal): +1 on avoiding 'permanent'. From a compliance POV we prefer specific retention periods and the ability to demonstrate deletion on request. Can we add an example retention policy snippet?

jess (Docs): Good call. Draft phrasing I'm thinking: "Exported audit records are retained for the configured retention period (default 90 days). Exports are encrypted with the customer's KMS key; when keys are rotated, previously encrypted exports remain decryptable provided the key versions are retained by the KMS. If a key is destroyed, exports encrypted with that key may become unrecoverable." Thoughts?

ben (DevEx): That reads well. For the SDK migration guide (v1 -> v2) we also need to update the example export command. Current sample is old CLI. Suggested replacement: 
```bash
# export recent audit events
ri audit export --start 2025-01-01 --end 2025-01-31 --kms-key my-key --output s3://company-exports/audit-january.ndjson
```
We should include both curl and python SDK examples.

sam (Eng): One edge-case: when we document 'logical tenant separation' vs 'physical separation' we need to be careful not to imply anything about guaranteed tenant isolation for Dedicated/Private setups. Maybe phrase as: "logical separation with access controls; Dedicated deployments can be configured with dedicated network/compute per customer."

maria (Legal): Yes, exact wording suggestion: "Data is logically partitioned by tenant within the Redwood service; Dedicated or Private deployments can provide additional physical and network isolation depending on contract and configuration."

jess (Docs): Perfect. I'll incorporate that. Two other tiny asks: 1) add short redaction guidance example for PII in exports, and 2) update links — current export page links to a retired internal runbook. Can @docs-bot post the new canonical runbook link?

docs-bot: New runbook link: https://go.redwood/runbooks/audit-exports (canonical). I've updated the link map in the docs repo (link-id: runbook-audit-exports). :white_check_mark:

omar (Security): For the redaction example, suggest showing a tiny transformation pipeline: 
```json
{"timestamp":"...","user_id":"[REDACTED]","action":"login_attempt"}
```
And mention that redaction should happen prior to export to minimize risk.

ben (DevEx): I'll add curl + python snippets. For python: 
```python
from redwood import AuditClient
client = AuditClient(api_key="$REDWOOD_API_KEY")
with client.export(start="2025-01-01", end="2025-01-31", kms_key="my-key") as stream:
    for line in stream:
        process(line)
```
Make sure we explain streaming vs batch exports.

jess (Docs): Great — I'm going to push an updated PR with all the changes (language tweaks, snippets, runbook link, redaction example). @maria @omar can you review legal/security bits once I push? Hoping for signoff today or tomorrow. :pray:

maria (Legal): Will review after lunch. If we need minor edits, I can approve wording quickly.

omar (Security): I'll do a security pass tonight and flag anything substantive. If nothing major, give me :thumbsup: and I'll mark as reviewed.

sam (Eng): FYI I'll update the dedicated-deploy FAQ to match the new sentence about physical isolation after the docs change lands.

docs-bot: PR 4567 status: open, reviewers requested: maria (Legal), omar (Security), ben (DevEx). CI: docs-lint passed, link-checker failed (old internal runbook links) — links updated by jess locally.

jess (Docs): Thanks all — I'll ping when PR is up with the new commits. Short and focused thread, feel free to add any micro-phrasing suggestions inline in the PR. :wave:
